A dragon skull mounted on an iron bracket above the mantle, its eye sockets packed with dried lavender and a single brass candle-stub flickering inside.
A glass alembic of dragon-glass with violet liquid bubbling slowly upward through a coiled copper neck into a receiving flask etched with containment runes.
A rolled celestial chart of aged vellum tied with crimson ribbon, partially unfurled across the low oak table, its star-positions annotated in faded silver ink.
A dragon-egg resting in a velvet-lined iron cradle, its surface mottled amber and obsidian, radiating a faint warmth detectable from across the room.
A tarnished silver compass on the windowsill with a cracked glass face, its needle spinning slowly rather than settling, enchanted and perpetually restless.
An open grimoire on a carved reading stand, its left page blazing with self-illuminating crimson script, the right page blank but visibly scorched at the margins.
A wooden rack of twelve apothecary bottles with hand-lettered parchment labels, three glowing faintly amber, one sealed with black wax stamped with a dragon sigil.
A deep wing-back armchair of burgundy leather with both arms worn pale and smooth, a folded wool blanket draped over one side, a cold teacup resting on its arm.
A taxidermied owl perched atop a brass rod above the bookshelf, its glass eyes catching candlelight, one outstretched talon gripping a preserved scroll-tube.
A dragon-scale display panel of aged rosewood framing seven iridescent scales pinned behind glass, each labeled in copperplate ink with territory and date of acquisition.
A small iron cauldron simmering on a trivet beside the hearth, releasing thin green steam that curls upward and briefly forms illegible rune-shapes before dispersing.
A brass oil-lantern hanging from a ceiling hook by a chain, burning blue flame rather than orange, casting cool cobalt shadows across the cluttered shelves beneath it.
A copper mortar stained deep green and rust-red from decades of herb grinding, its wooden pestle resting across the rim, a dusting of dried powder coating the lip.
A rune-carved oak chest with wide iron strap-bands, its lid slightly ajar, from which spills a fold of heavy crimson cloth and the glint of something golden inside.
A cracked terrestrial globe on a tarnished brass meridian ring, one continent crossed out in red ink, a handwritten correction inked beside it in a cramped scholarly hand.
A wall-pinned map of the northern ranges with red silk string connecting seven circled locations, three marked with small wax dragon seals pressed flat against the parchment.
A glass jar of preserved specimen on the middle shelf, its contents floating in pale amber liquid, identifiable as a tiny scaled claw no larger than a thumb, label unreadable.
A dragon-tooth letter-opener of yellowed ivory resting across an ink-stained blotter, its handle wrapped in braided copper wire and engraved with a single glyph near the base.
A bundle of dried herbs bound with twine and hanging from a ceiling rafter, its lower leaves dusty and curling, casting a faint herbal shadow on the parchments below.
A cluttered roll-top desk of dark oak with the tambour half-open, revealing stacked correspondence, a burnt-edged map, three quills, and a spilled pot of dried black ink.
A crystal orb the size of a fist resting on a wrought-iron tripod stand, its interior pulsing with slow amber light in a rhythm that subtly matches the room's candle-flicker.
A gilded chess set mid-game on the low side table, several pieces knocked over, a leather-bound chess notation book open beside it with the last recorded move circled twice.
A multi-arm candelabra of wrought iron with nine arms and twenty years of cascading wax built into pale sculptural ridges along the central column, four remaining flames lit.
A glass vial rack of carved walnut holding eleven vials of glowing liquids in separate colors, one vial stoppered with wax and labeled in red ink: DO NOT OPEN INDOORS.
A sextant of tarnished brass resting on the window ledge beside an open shutter, its arc engraved with constellation names, a single dried ink-mark on the index arm.
